fatal_errors: The proposed sulfur- or phosphorus-doped HEA does not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiMox–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite or the controlled variation of Mo content.

The stated -200 to 1000 °C and 0 to 1000 MPa operating boundaries are invented and unsupported; the target concerns dry sliding in air from room temperature to 800 °C under a specific 8 N ball-on-disk condition.

The hypothesis omits the central strengthening and lubrication mechanisms: Mo-induced lattice distortion, Mo-rich sigma-phase formation, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation.
No evidence is cited for sulfur or phosphorus preserving strength or producing wide-temperature lubrication.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad goal of combining HEA mechanical strength with self-lubrication, but it substitutes a generic and unevidenced sulfur/phosphorus-alloying proposal for the target material system. It does not identify the multicomponent CoCrFeNiMox composite, the Mo-content comparison, SPS processing, temperature-dependent wear regimes, or the experimentally observed advantage of Mo1 at 800 °C. Its proposed test is directionally falsifiable but lacks defined compositions, counterface, load, speed, atmosphere, and quantitative acceptance criteria, so it cannot sharply discriminate the target mechanism.
